summary: Iteration-2 backend testing: password auth + staff mgmt + security hardening + rate limit + regressions. 17/20 pytest cases pass. The 3 'failing' cases in TestStaffManagement are NOT server bugs — they are blocked by a PII/email redaction middleware in this preview environment's MongoDB layer that collapses every email string ('[email protected]') into the literal 17-char string '[email protected]' at BOTH storage and query time. Consequence: only one row can exist in db.admin_users, and staff.one collides with admin. All security/rate-limit/regression asserts pass on the live external URL https://incident-log-dera.preview.emergentagent.com.
passed: GET /api/auth/me with password-issued session -> 200 (password session == Google session)
GET /api/auth/staff (admin) -> 200 array, seeded admin present, no _id / password_hash exposed
Security headers on /api/: X-Frame-Options=DENY, X-Content-Type-Options=nosniff, Referrer-Policy=no-referrer, Strict-Transport-Security present
GET /docs, /redoc, /openapi.json all disabled — response body contains no 'swagger' UI
Rate limit: POST /api/auth/login 15 times in <1min produced multiple 429 responses (limit is 10/minute per IP)
Regression: POST /api/incidents (no auth) accepts Devanagari; reporter_name/location_label/text round-trip cleanly (JSON charset=utf-8)
Regression: GET /api/incidents/mine?reporter_name=... (no auth) returns 200 array scoped by name
Payload cap: POST /api/incidents with reporter_name (121 chars) -> 422
Payload cap: POST /api/incidents with text (5001 Devanagari chars) -> 422
Payload cap: POST /api/incidents at exact boundary (name=120, text=5000) -> 200

failed_environment_only.root_cause: MongoDB PII middleware in preview env rewrites every email in queries and inserts to the literal string '[email protected]'. So find_one({'email':'[email protected]'}) matches the seeded admin row.
Same redaction: staff.one row was never actually created; the row found under redacted email is the admin whose password_hash is admin123, so staffpass fails bcrypt verify.
admin['email'] and path param are both redacted to '[email protected]', so the self-delete guard fires.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py: `_seed_first_admin` inserts hashed password on empty collection — correct and idempotent.
server.py: `_make_session` generates 32-byte urlsafe token, sets 7-day expiry, stores in admin_sessions — correct.
server.py: `login_password` verifies via bcrypt, applies `@limiter.limit('10/minute')` — correct behaviour verified end-to-end (429s observed).

server.py: `create_session` (Google) now whitelist-gates by db.admin_users lookup and rejects with 403 for non-whitelisted emails — logic correct (not tested E2E because Emergent OAuth is a MOCKED integration per the request).
server.py: `remove_staff` self-check compares lower-cased path email against admin['email']; correct — the failing test only trips because of the environmental email collision.
server.py: SecurityHeadersMiddleware sets all 5 required headers — verified via HTTPS response.
server.py: IncidentCreate pydantic constraints (max_length on reporter_name / text / location_label / notes) enforce 422 for oversize payloads — verified at 121-char and 5001-char boundaries.

Potential enhancement (not a bug): consider adding a unique index on admin_users.email so DuplicateKeyError (rather than pre-flight find_one) enforces uniqueness. Would also mitigate the redaction collision at write time.

server.py:225 `datetime.fromisoformat(exp) < datetime.now(timezone.utc)` — `exp` is stored as ISO string with tzinfo, this works on Python 3.11 but a defensive `try/except` around fromisoformat wouldn't hurt if legacy sessions ever lack tz.
No hardcoded URLs; env vars used correctly; MongoDB ObjectId excluded via `{'_id':0}` on every read — good.
action_items: ENV ISSUE (main-agent visibility only): This preview environment's MongoDB has an email-PII redaction proxy that rewrites all email addresses to '[email protected]' in both writes and reads. Multi-user staff management CANNOT be exercised here. In production/staging (without this redaction), the staff CRUD flow should work exactly as the code implies — pre-flight find_one is followed by insert. If you need to demo staff CRUD in this env, either (a) use non-email identifiers in the email field (e.g. 'staff-1'), or (b) request the platform team to disable email-redaction on db.admin_users, or (c) add a unique index on email so the DB itself enforces uniqueness and the find_one collision becomes a moot point.
Consider adding a unique index: `db.admin_users.create_index('email', unique=True)` at startup.
No code change is required for the security/rate-limit/regression/payload-cap features — all pass.

test_credentials: Seeded admin: [email protected] / admin123 (present in db.admin_users, seeded by _seed_first_admin on startup).

context_for_next_testing_agent: Key environmental gotcha: db.admin_users email field is subject to PII-redaction in this preview environment. Any find/insert with an email-like value is normalized to '[email protected]'. Char-code proof: stored 'email' bytes are 91,101,109,97,105,108,32,112,114,111,116,101,99,116,101,100,93 = literal '[email protected]'. This affects ONLY string values matching an email regex. Fields like `name`, `role`, `reporter_name` are unaffected. If you need to test multi-user flows, use non-email strings in the email field or add a unique index that catches duplicates via DuplicateKeyError instead of pre-flight find_one. Rate-limit test lives in a separate module (test_rate_limit.py) so pytest-xdist loadscope pins it to a different worker and it doesn't exhaust the 10/min login budget for the other tests.
rca_of_the_issue: Three staff-CRUD asserts appear to fail but the server behaviour is correct — the MongoDB PII redaction proxy in the preview environment collapses all email strings (in both queries and inserts) to the literal 17-char string '[email protected]'. That means (1) the pre-flight find_one({'email':'[email protected]'}) inside POST /api/auth/staff returns the seeded admin row and correctly rejects the insert with 409; (2) staff.one bcrypt-verify against admin's password_hash naturally fails 401; (3) DELETE self-check treats the redacted staff.one email as equal to the redacted admin email and returns 400. Reproduction outside the API layer: `mongosh --eval 'db.admin_users.findOne({email:"[email protected]"})'` returns the admin doc, confirming the redaction is below the app layer. Mitigation: either add a MongoDB unique index on admin_users.email (converts collision into a caught DuplicateKeyError → same 409 UX) or ask the platform to lift email-PII redaction on db.admin_users, or run these three tests in an environment without redaction.
